title: Hush up? Development of an expanded questionnaire for assessing expectations of end-of-life conversations among informal caregivers
summary: Although death is a natural part of life, talking about the end of life is often avoided in today’s society. We are examining why loved ones often shy away from such conversations. In previous studies, we developed questionnaires on expectations regarding conversations about the end of life, from the perspectives of both those affected and their relatives. The focus so far has been on negative expectations, while positive expectations have been overlooked. The aim of the current study is to develop a questionnaire focusing on both negative and positive expectations. This time, the survey will target family caregivers.
conditions: No specific illness; family caregivers are recruited (family caregivers are defined as relatives or friends who care for patients without compensation and assist them with physically, emotionally, and socially demanding tasks)

interventions.name:
A one-time online survey (paper-and-pencil questionnaires and anonymous return envelopes are also available upon request) to validate a newly developed questionnaire designed to assess the expectations of family caregivers regarding end-of-life conversations
